I'm sixty this year, and I've been farming these fields for forty-five years. My family has 10.9 mu of land in Quzhou County. Seven mu is in wheat-maize double cropping, and the remaining 3.9 mu is for cotton. Seven of us live under one roof, but my son and daughter-in-law work off-farm in the county town. They come back for harvest and planting rush, but day-to-day it's me and my wife handling things.

The winter wheat went in last October. Now it's early spring, and I need to think about the topdressing. The extension agent says I should put on 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, but last year I pushed to 10 kg at green-up and the wheat lodged badly in that thunderstorm. So this year I'm being more careful — I'll topdress about 7 kg of urea per mu at green-up, and if the wheat looks strong at jointing, maybe another 3 kg. That brings my total N to about 14 kg per mu, counting what I put down last autumn. I'll irrigate three times: once at green-up to help the fertilizer along, once at jointing, and once at grain filling if May is dry. Irrigation costs money — every time I turn on that pump the electric meter spins — but three times is the minimum for decent wheat here. I'll spray twice: herbicide early, and fungicide for head scab around heading. I'm hoping for 420 kg per mu if the weather holds, which is a bit below what the young guys get, but I'm farming conservatively.

Summer maize has to go in right after wheat harvest — three days, maybe five if the weather is bad, but every day you delay costs yield. I buy hybrid seed from the dealer, about 55 yuan per mu. I don't deep-till between wheat and maize; there's no time. I broadcast the seed and work it in shallow. Base fertilizer goes down with planting, then I topdress urea at the big trumpet stage. Two irrigations: one when the plants are knee-high, and one around tasseling. If July is wet, I might skip the second one and save 250 yuan in pumping costs. But I'm budgeting for both, because drought at tasseling means disaster. Yield target is 450 kg per mu.

Cotton gets planted in late April on the 3.9 mu. Cotton is different — it needs more attention and more chemicals. I'll put down base fertilizer and bed the rows properly. Then side-dress at flowering and again at boll stage. Total N around 10 kg per mu, less than the grain crops because cotton is more sensitive to excess nitrogen — makes it grow leaves instead of bolls. I'll irrigate twice. Pesticide is where cotton gets expensive: at least three sprays for bollworm, plus something for aphids, plus herbicide. That's probably 120 yuan per mu just for chemicals. The real bottleneck is picking. My wife and I can't do it alone — we need my son and daughter-in-law back for the first picking in September, and we'll probably hire five days of labor too. Hoping for 230 kg of lint per mu.

Money is tight. Total input costs will run about 7,900 yuan this year. I don't have that sitting in cash all at once, so I'll buy the wheat fertilizer now, the cotton seed and chemicals in April, and the maize seed in May. I'd rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk a bad year — losing half a crop hurts a lot more than saving a few hundred yuan on inputs.
